title: iac-compose implementation contract
description: Customer-specific handoff from Azure workload intent recognition to iac-compose infrastructure authoring.

solution.description: Stable identity for the complete workload solution.

name.description: Stable solution name; environment names are separate deployment parameters.

profile.description: Workload criticality profile that controls baseline reliability, security, operations, performance, and cost decisions.

authoringMode.description: Final iac-compose authoring route for the complete resource graph.

components.description: Deployable application units and lifecycle owners.

resources.description: Azure services and logical resources required by the workload.

parameters.description: Deployment input declarations; parameter values are never stored in this contract.

dependencies.description: Producer-to-consumer resource edges established through nonsecret outputs.

deploymentOrder.description: Ordered component IDs and explicit shared-layer IDs.

assumptions.description: Evidence-qualified architecture decisions and reversible defaults.

wellArchitected.description: Workload-specific requirements for all five Azure Well-Architected Framework pillars.

reliability.description: Failure, availability, backup, restore, and recovery requirements.

security.description: Identity, least privilege, secret, encryption, and exposure requirements.

costOptimization.description: Capacity, elasticity, retention, and avoidable-cost requirements.

operationalExcellence.description: Deployment, observability, release, and incident-response requirements.

performanceEfficiency.description: Scaling, concurrency, quota, partitioning, and latency requirements.

tradeoffs.description: Explicitly accepted costs or risks and their revisit triggers.

benefit.description: Quality, capability, or simplicity gained by the choice.

cost.description: Money, complexity, latency, availability, or risk introduced.

revisitTrigger.description: Measurable event that requires reconsidering the choice.

validation.description: Measurable local and deployment-time validation gates.

stage.description: Whether the gate runs without Azure side effects or against deployment context.

check.description: Specific validation that must be performed.

unresolved.description: Blocking architecture decisions; this array must be empty before implementation.

decision.description: Decision or required input that remains unresolved.

impact.description: Why implementation cannot proceed safely without resolving it.

nonEmptyStrings.description: One or more non-empty requirement statements.

component.description: Deployable application unit or lifecycle owner.

kind.description: Component role, such as http-api, worker, static-site, or hosted-agent.

source.description: Application source directory relative to the solution package.

runtime.description: Runtime family, such as node, python, container, or static.

protocol.description: Primary component interface, such as https, grpc, queue, or none.

lifecycle.description: Execution shape, such as request-driven, event-driven, scheduled, or batch.

resource.description: Azure service or logical infrastructure resource required by the workload.

capability.description: Workload requirement satisfied by this resource.

requiredBy.description: Component IDs that require this resource.

ownership.description: Whether the resource belongs to one component or a shared provisioning layer.

implementation.description: Discriminated authoring route for this resource.

oneOf.description: Translate this resource into a supported iac-compose resource kind.
Implement this resource through direct TypeScript provisioning.

azureResourceTypes.description: Provider-qualified ARM resource types required to implement the capability and controls.

configuration.description: Kind- or service-specific desired configuration without secret values.

controls.description: Testable security, reliability, cost, operations, and performance requirements.

produces.description: Nonsecret logical outputs made available to other resources or lifecycle steps.

consumes.description: Logical outputs required from other declared resources.

principalOutput.description: Logical principal ID output produced by another declared resource.

role.description: Least-privilege role or explicit post-provisioning access operation.

parameter.description: Deployment input declaration without an embedded value.

name.description: Environment variable or deployment parameter name.

required.description: Whether generation or deployment can proceed without the input.

secret.description: Whether the value requires secret storage and redaction.

reason.description: Why the workload requires the input.

dependency.description: Output-based ordering edge between two declared resources.

producer.description: Resource ID that produces the output.

consumer.description: Resource ID that consumes the output.

via.description: Logical output name connecting producer and consumer.

assumption.description: Evidence-qualified architecture decision or reversible default.

evidence.description: Prompt, repository, existing infrastructure, or workload-profile evidence.

confidence.description: Strength and origin of the conclusion.

revisitTrigger.description: Event or threshold that requires reconsidering the decision.
